items.summary_html: Anthropic is grappling with balancing bold safety initiatives and disappointing operational decisions. CEO Dario Amodei has defended their costly, safety-oriented strategies, yet concerns persist over alignment, governance, and potential risks from AI development. Their internal culture reflects both ambitious efforts and troubling signs of a conventional business approach, sparking debate about their commitment to AI safety and global responsibilities.
items.title: Anthropic Versus Anthropic (17 minute read)

items.summary_html: Axiom Math has released the first complete computer-checked proof of the Classification of Finite Simple Groups (CFSG). The original CFSG proof is considered to be the longest mathematical proof ever written by humans. It spans roughly 15,000 pages in more than 500 articles written by about 100 mathematicians. Engineers and mathematicians at Axiom Math directed swarms of dozens of AI agents over 24 days in a project that produced approximately 43.1 million lines of code in the Lean proof assistant.
items.title: Formalizing the Enormous Theorem (27 minute read)

items.summary_html: The AI Chip Imports explorer estimates AI compute arrivals by country since 2022, enhancing the mapping of the global AI chip supply chain. It complements existing data on AI chip components, sales, and data centers. These resources collectively provide a detailed overview of AI compute allocation and control worldwide.
items.title: Where are the world's AI chips? (1 minute read)

items.summary_html: StreamVibe-VL is a vision-language model that infers implicit user intentions from continuous observations and adapts as those intentions change.
items.title: Proactive Video Agents (22 minute read)

items.summary_html: Researchers have developed a new way to enable large language models to integrate new facts and enhance reasoning without catastrophic forgetting or static knowledge cutoffs. The sleep framework equips large language models with a continuous periodic lifecycle, enabling them to continually learn and consolidate fragile short-term context into stable long-term parameters. Alternating between active interaction and offline memory consolidation allows LLMs to continuously acquire new facts, retain long-context knowledge up to 10M tokens, and improve complex reasoning.
items.title: The sleep framework: A new way for LLMs to retain knowledge in continual learning (11 minute read)

items.summary_html: FrontierCode 2.0 provides broader coverage, higher mergeability standards, and a larger task scope while largely retaining the methodology of FrontierCode 1.0. The benchmark now accommodates surprising but acceptable behavior. Tasks are drawn from more repositories and span more categories, and grading criteria now impose more extensive correctness and design requirements. Reference solutions now modify 67% more files and 89% more lines of code on average compared to FrontierCode 1.1, in codebases that are 25% larger.
items.title: FrontierCode 2.0 (13 minute read)

items.summary_html: InteractiveWorld is a simulation framework for training and evaluating wearable AI assistants. It models interactions where an assistant observes through a user's eyes, communicates with them, and receives updated first-person views.
items.title: Meta's Interactive Simulator for Wearable AI (GitHub Repo)

items.summary_html: Anthropic says an internal research Claude model found, with no human input, a deterministic algorithm that counts the satisfying assignments of 3-SAT formulas in 2^O(n log log n/√log n) time, which would make 3-SAT subexponential and refute ETH. This repository holds the paper and a Lean 4 formalization written by AI models that builds in about 8 minutes, though Anthropic notes no machine checks that the Lean statement matches the paper and the result says nothing about practical SAT solving. It landed hours after OpenAI's own ETH refutation.
items.title: Anthropic's Claude Refutes the Exponential Time Hypothesis, With a Lean Proof (GitHub Repo)

items.summary_html: Anthropic partnered with six pharmaceutical and biotechnology organizations to explore how Claude could accelerate drug development, from early research to clinical trial preparation. It also launched internal drug discovery programs targeting rare childhood diseases, with Claude handling substantial scientific and operational work.
items.title: Anthropic's Drug Development Process (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Anthropic has acquired a one-person biotech run by Cody Tranbarger. Mithril Medicine is a startup founded to develop cures for diseases using AI. Joining Anthropic means Mithril will be able to continue running its programs with more resources, and it will allow Tranbarger to start several more programs. They aim to scale the startup's new way of working, then put it in the hands of all biopharma, all over the world.
items.title: Anthropic acquired a one-person biotech (4 minute read)

items.title: Compare Commits to Your Code, Resolve Conflicts in Bulk, Keep Coding (5 minute read)

Google says its eighth-generation TPU delivers up to 12.6 PFLOPS of FP4 per chip at up to 2x performance per watt, sustains over 97% goodput with optical circuit switching, and cuts network hops by over 50% for up to 80% better low-latency serving performance per dollar.
items.title: Oracle Cloud becomes the first hyperscaler outside Google to offer TPUs, with capacity from 2027 (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Big Iron is an 86 m stainless-steel, road-transportable rocket that can carry 15,000+ kg to sun-synchronous orbit on nine 300,000 lbf methalox ‘Clydesdale' engines. The upper stage can stay in orbit as a data center with five racks of Vera Rubin GPUs, with the rocket skin doubling as the radiator and ammonia propellant as coolant. Its first flight is targeted for 2028, with up to 20,000 satellites planned pending FCC approval.
items.title: Cowboy Space's Big Iron rocket turns its upper stage into an orbiting megawatt-class data center (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: BlueChip runs a Snapdragon X Series chip built at TSMC's Arizona fab, with about 90% of its bill of materials from the US or allies and a roadmap to 100% domestic. The display is one component still made only in China. It's aimed at government and military buyers rather than consumers. The chip is expected to cost about 20% more than typical high-end PCs, and open for preorder in 2027. Anduril hasn't finished contracting its suppliers.
items.title: Anduril and Qualcomm announce BlueChip, a hardened laptop with about 90% US or allied parts (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: The push for silicon photonics in data centers requires testing infrastructure that matches evolving demands. Automated alignment and integrated optical/electrical testing are critical for overcoming challenges in coupling efficiency and throughput. Collaboration between equipment providers, developers, and manufacturers is essential to create a seamless production system for high-volume manufacturing.
items.title: Testing Silicon Photonics At Scale (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: A theory paper proposes reading an Andreev qubit without ancilla qubits: its state shows up as an oscillating supercurrent in a large superconducting loop, and a small coil coupled to a SQUID picks up the magnetic signal. The method still disturbs the qubit, but within standard error-correction thresholds. It's a proposal in Physical Review B, supported by FAPESP, with no experiment yet.
items.title: Proposal reads an Andreev qubit's state through its supercurrent and a SQUID, with no ancilla qubits (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Renesas has launched the RX74M and RX74N, the first 32-bit MCUs using a 22nm process with embedded MRAM, reaching speeds up to 600MHz. These MCUs offer significant performance improvements and support major industrial networks like EtherCAT and TSN with integrated controllers. They enhance security with hardware-based features and support post-quantum cryptography, while a partner ecosystem aids development efficiency.
items.title: First 32-bit MCU family built on 22nm process and featuring MRAM (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: The fusion industry is close to delivering a roadmap to commercial power plants. The fuel cycle, especially tritium handling, is one of the most important development areas.
items.title: Fusion's supply chain could grow from $500M to over $7B by the first plants, with the tritium fuel cycle the key hurdle (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Intel has agreed to acquire Classiq, pairing its hardware-agnostic algorithm synthesis platform with Intel's silicon spin-qubit chips and cryogenic control electronics, which Intel says it alone can make at scale on conventional fab processes. The goal is a full-stack platform that adds QPUs alongside Intel's CPUs, GPUs, and ASICs. Intel plans to keep Classiq's multi-platform integrations.
items.title: Intel to acquire quantum software maker Classiq to pair it with silicon spin-qubit chips (2 minute read)

A broader release will be available after Google improves guardrails on the model based on feedback. Carbon will launch at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, with a 95% discount for cached inputs. items.summary_html: The new MacBook Pro has an OLED touchscreen display. The display can achieve 2,000 nits of maximum brightness, and Apple claims it has a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio. The new laptop is lighter than the previous model at just 3 pounds. The top-of-screen camera notch has been replaced by a Dynamic Island, and the Apple logo on the back of the lid glows like in older models.
items.title: Apple announces touchscreen MacBook Pro with OLED display (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Apeiron, a Delta-class suborbital spacecraft from Virgin Galactic, is being moved from Virgin Galactic's Spaceship Factory in Mesa, Arizona, to Spaceport America in New Mexico. After its arrival, aircraft engineers and technicians will complete work on the vehicle's avionics equipment and flight software. Apeiron will still require several ground tests and test flights before it can make a free flight. Virgin Galactic expects Apeiron's first commercial spaceflight to take place early in the second quarter of 2027.
items.title: The last, best hope for space tourism just rolled onto a runway in Arizona (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: The Grid is a factory-scale robot that can build circuit boards on demand. Every board takes its own route through the factory, which has machines that print solder paste, place parts, reflow, solder, and inspect. With The Grid, printing one unit of 100 designs is as easy as printing 100 units of one, and prototypes and production batches run on the same machines. It allows companies to manufacture huge numbers of low-volume boards, and could help bring manufacturing back to the US.
items.title: Unveiling The Grid: PCBs made in America, twice as fast as Shenzhen (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Models have been able to create something that looks like a game for a while, but the games weren't fun. The latest generation of models exhibit meaningful improvements in game design, allowing them to create games with novel, compelling gameplay loops. The challenge now is coming up with concepts for games that wouldn't exist without AI assistance.
items.title: The October inflection point for vibe game development (13 minute read)

items.summary_html: The Slack Code API allows agents to start code channels, add relevant people and files, post updates as they work, and archive channels when the work is done. It enables teams to work together with agents on tasks with the same shared context. Users can see exactly what agents are doing and who approved it, and workspace controls and data boundaries are built in. Users can choose what agents and models they want to use to suit their needs.
items.title: Introducing the Slack Code API: Your agents, your team, one code channel (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: It is now possible to build a highly profitable business with significant scale without raising or hiring a ton. Founders can take advantage of new AI tools to generate financial freedom and build organizations to work on the things they want to, with the people they want, at a scale, ambition, and pace that works for them. This article explores how the founders of turbopuffer, a startup that powers the search infrastructure for many AI companies, built their company. It explores what life and work in the time of AI can look like, and shows how ambitious builders and founders can try it for themselves.

items.summary_html: Reddit's redesigned feed is designed to nudge users to engage with content beyond the communities they already follow.
items.title: Reddit is the latest platform to embrace the ‘For You' feed (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Next.js 16.4 adds an agent skill that uses Turbopack's module graph to find unnecessary client JavaScript, including eager imports, duplicate dependencies, and missed tree shaking. Vercel reports removing or deferring nearly two megabytes of compressed JavaScript across pages in v0 and vercel.com, with snapshot comparisons to verify each change.
items.title: Ship less JavaScript in Next.js with your AI agent (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: typed-channel defines message names and payloads once so TypeScript can check both sides of a worker, iframe, or event-bus boundary. The core plus postMessage transport is 341 bytes with Brotli compression, while a separate request API adds typed replies and cancellation that propagates to the handler.
items.title: How to make postMessage type-safe in under 350 bytes (9 minute read)

items.summary_html: Local-first can mean offline capability, fast optimistic interfaces, or user ownership of data, and those promises lead to different architectures. Hologram prioritizes responsive local interfaces and offline support while retaining a server to enforce permissions and business rules.
items.title: Local-First Means Three Different Things (9 minute read)

items.summary_html: A benchmark asks Opus 5.5 to build the same Pokémon app across JavaScript frameworks, then measures cost, time, spec compliance, performance, and accessibility over repeated runs. Hono with htmx, Astro, and Nuxt are among the cheapest in this experiment, but substantial run-to-run variance and a mostly content-focused app limit how broadly the ranking applies.
items.title: The AI cost of JavaScript frameworks (15 minute read)

items.summary_html: AI agents could make technical website migrations nearly free by using the existing site as a baseline for differential tests of pages and publishing workflows. The prediction shifts the durable sources of lock-in toward contracts, procurement approvals, and agent memory, making portable requirements and decision logs more valuable.
items.title: Website migration costs are going to zero (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Nuxt DevTools v4 moves onto the framework-agnostic Devframe and Vite DevTools foundations, allowing it to reuse the Vite and Vue tooling ecosystem. A transition shim supports legacy modules while their integrations migrate to the new Devframe APIs.
items.title: Nuxt DevTools v4 (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon for sustained coding workflows and cybersecurity, reporting 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro for vulnerability discovery and 71.0% on CWE-bench for patching. Access begins with selected cyber defenders and trusted Fairwind partners, with broader availability still to come. Announced introductory pricing is $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens.
items.title: Gemini 4 Carbon: our next frontier model (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: Vercel CI enters beta with Turborepo-based task selection and remote caching, running only work affected by a code change. Vercel reports two to six times faster push-to-passed-check times while reducing the need for separate CI workflow configuration.
items.title: Introducing Vercel CI (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Opus 5.5 has improved at generating 3D models, music, and gameplay that is fun to play. Simple instructions can produce working games. More ambitious projects still need playtesting and iteration to fix gameplay problems.
items.title: The October inflection point for vibe game development (10 minute read)

items.summary_html: During a model comparison at Funnel, an internal data agent repeatedly executed a successful SQL query instead of finishing its task. The failure illustrates why model swaps need whole-system evaluation, explicit tool contracts, and bounds on repeated behavior.
items.title: Our AI Agent Executed the Same Successful SQL Query 254 Times (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: A browser fingerprinting script hides alarming prompts and variable names intended to trip LLM safety filters and frustrate automated analysis. Underneath the anti-LLM obfuscation, it collects conventional browser and WebGL signals and includes a gated Node.js routine for gathering system information.
items.title: Why Is This Fingerprinting Script Creating Bioweapons? (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: Ghostty 1.4 adds complete Kitty graphics support, scrollback compression, faster terminal processing, improved SSH integration, and security fixes.
items.title: Ghostty 1.4 (Website)

items.summary_html: Node.js 26 has entered Long Term Support as Lithium through April 2029.
items.title: Node.js 26.13.0 enters LTS (1 minute read)

items.summary_html: Yavashark is an embeddable Rust JavaScript engine that passes 82% of test262 and supports Temporal, Intl, and TypeScript execution through its CLI.
items.title: Yavashark: a new embeddable JavaScript engine in Rust (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: A decompression error in affected body-parser versions can crash a server with one request.
items.title: Denial of service in body-parser (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Google has introduced the Gemini 4 Carbon model, advancing AI capabilities with improved energy efficiency. This model enhances performance in natural language processing tasks while reducing carbon footprint, addressing sustainability concerns in AI development. Gemini 4 Carbon aims to set new industry standards for eco-friendly AI models.
items.title: Gemini 4 Carbon (1 minute read)

items.summary_html: NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe is an open-weight model for multilingual transcription, translation, speaker attribution, and audio Q&A. It's ranked first across several transcription and speaker attribution leaderboards, supporting up to 40 languages with low error rates. Granary v2 enhances this by offering reusable data pipelines and fine-tuning options, enabling customization for diverse vocabularies and specialized applications.
items.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe and Granary v2: Intelligent Multilingual Transcription You Can Prompt and Adapt (14 minute read)

items.summary_html: Decagon's AutoResearch agents diagnose inference bottlenecks, test optimizations against production traffic replays, and preserve findings across experiments. The company reports throughput gains up to 2.5x within endpoint latency requirements through quantization, scheduling, engine patches, and speculative decoding, with production changes requiring human approval.
items.title: Building an Inference Stack That Improves Itself (20 minute read)

items.summary_html: Independent evaluation of language models is a hard task. It is difficult to create a number that is representative of current models that matches vibe checks, community sentiment, and scientific analysis, while being forward-looking enough so that it's not outdated in three months. Independent evaluators dictate the winners and losers of a trillion-dollar market. They can also influence the direction of model development, increasing the pressure.
items.title: Artificial Analysis v5 and the benchmarker's dilemma (11 minute read)

items.summary_html: Qwenputer is a fully functioning, deterministic RISC-V CPU that runs inside Qwen3.5. The CPU runs on its own Gated DeltaNet layers as RAM. It can run arithmetic operations and C and MicroPython code without any external runtime or tool usage. This post explains how the model works, how the model uses GDN layers as RAM, and how the developer also slotted in an experimental in-model file storage.
items.title: Qwenputer: a fully functioning, deterministic RISC-V CPU inside Qwen3.5 (9 minute read)

items.summary_html: The Vercel AI is now available in beta. The CI is able to keep up with coding agents. It runs only the tasks affected by a code change, and spins up only the compute those checks need. At Vercel, the system has decreased the time from git push to 'CI pass' by 2-6x.
items.title: Introducing Vercel CI (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: GitHub Copilot Fusion lets Copilot intelligently route and orchestrate models for each task. It leverages the benefits of Project HydraFusion's multi-model orchestration and Copilot auto model selection's fine-tuned model selection to balance performance and cost efficiency. Copilot Fusion determines which models to use and how they work together depending on the level of effort selected by the user. Administrators can control which models Copilot Fusion can use and whether Copilot Fusion is the default.
items.title: Route and orchestrate models with GitHub Copilot Fusion (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: The Microsoft Copilot harness powers Copilot Code, Copilot Studio, the GitHub Copilot app, the CLI, VS Code, and more. It is now available through Microsoft Foundry. The harness gives developers and enterprise customers a fully managed way to build agents that reason, use tools, and complete complex, long-running tasks. It was built to perform across model families, and is flexible and configurable to any type of app, agent, or service.
items.title: Introducing the Microsoft Copilot harness: Unlocking the potential of truly multi-model agentic work (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Anthropic has launched reporting tools to help companies measure and optimize their AI spending with its products like Claude Code. The tools offer detailed insights on productivity, costs, and recommendations, addressing a major concern for enterprise clients. Despite competition from models like OpenAI's Astra, Anthropic's strong enterprise presence and sticky workflows continue to drive significant adoption and spending growth.
items.title: Anthropic just launched tools to show companies what their AI spending is buying (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: Meta launched Waddle World, a virtual AI pet app that functions like a Tamagotchi, in the Philippines on iOS and Android. Unlike traditional productivity tools or chatbots, it serves as a digital pet and personal journal, allowing users to interact and play mini-games without pressure. The app reflects Meta's cautious approach following legal issues faced by other AI companion apps.
items.title: Meta has a new AI pet app called Waddle World (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Google has introduced a centralized platform for building and managing connected apps.
items.title: Build and manage Connected Apps in one place (1 minute read)

items.summary_html: ElevenLabs' Cue is a forced alignment model for precise character-level timing in audio files.
items.title: ElevenLabs Cue: Character-level audio timing (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: Lor is a system with agents that write code, run experiments, and iterate for days across hundreds of parallel workers.
items.title: Mirendil Introduces Lor for AI Research Automation (1 minute read)

items.summary_html: OpenAI now allows US Pro users to text their Dot agents via iMessage and RCS, enabling instructions through text, photos, and voice memos.
items.title: OpenAI now lets you text your Dot agent (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Copilot Automations now self-improve by learning from real-world outcomes on GitHub.
items.title: Copilot Automations now learn from outcomes and self-improve (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: DoorDash will acquire Instacart for $17 billion. Instacart shareholders will receive $65 per share, 26% over the company's price on October 22. Combining the companies' technology and infrastructure will result in faster deliveries and more affordable prices. The deal is expected to close late next year or in 2028.
items.title: DoorDash to Buy Instacart for $17 Billion, Uniting 2 Delivery Giants (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: Reddit will start testing a logged-in-only experience in select non-US markets in Q4. The company's CEO says the login requirement will help Reddit retain new users. It will also provide more signals for ads targeting and help protect access to the site's data. The changes will make it significantly easier for Reddit to understand who uses Reddit and why, which will help the site manage things like AI scraping and evolving search habits.
items.title: Reddit is moving to “a logged-in-only experience,” CEO says (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Progress has started to accelerate in science in the last two years. AI can send hordes of superhumanly fast, well-read, and mathematically gifted researchers to accelerate scientific research. It is possible AI will enable new types of discovery and ways of understanding the natural world that no network of humans would ever be able to discover. Unless humans have actually somehow discovered most of the actual exploitable regularities in the Universe, we're about to enter a new golden age of science.
items.title: A golden age of science is coming (16 minute read)

items.summary_html: Neuralink's Blindsight implant is now ready from an engineering standpoint. The device is designed to help blind people see. It is currently waiting on regulatory approval before it can be sold to customers. It has already received Breakthrough Device Designation from the US FDA, which will help speed review of the device.
items.title: Elon Says Blindsight Is Ready 2 Years After FDA Breakthrough (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Adding constraints to AI agents usually makes them less capable. Sometimes the solution is to create a template or a complete multi-stage workflow. The challenge is in creating the deterministic behavior while retaining the agent's freedom to use the best tools for the job. This post discusses a solution that uses a man-in-the-middle egress proxy that forces behavior by denying actions and forces reactions via automated messages.
items.title: A Little Determinism (16 minute read)

items.summary_html: Knowing what part of inference a project relies on for speed is important. Check thinking budgets, and read traces, as they often contain valuable insight into what an agent wants to do. Give agents the tools they want rather than what you think they need. Faster hardware still matters, sandboxing and microVMs add complexity, parallelization helps, and classic software performance optimization is still relevant.
items.title: Making agents fast - what I've learnt over the last 12 months (12 minute read)

items.summary_html: Binance has suspended transactions after a hack that the exchange said totaled around $6.3 billion. Stablecoin providers Tether and Circle moved quickly to freeze some of the stolen assets. The heist appears to have been conducted by a North Korean hacking group. Binance's founder said in a post on social media that users' funds are safe.
items.title: Binance Suspends Transactions After It Is Targeted in Biggest-Ever Cyber Heist (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: The standard answer for what humans will do after the Singularity is that people 'will just hang out'. However, AI will destroy the processes by which people come together and build relationships. With unlimited entertainment, people might not even want to socialize with other people. The people in the AI utopia will have no skills, education, or accomplishments, so they'll likely not be worth talking to, and you probably wouldn't want to hang out with them.
items.title: We Won't “Just Hang Out” (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: If you want to communicate with humans, your humanity has to be visible in your prose.
items.title: LLM Voice (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: The Commanding Heights are scarce, controllable positions of economic power whose holders durably capture the gains of increasingly capable and diffused intelligence.
items.title: The Commanding Heights (Book)

items.title: Nvidia Chief Seen as Target of Chinese Spy Plot (18 minute read)

items.summary_html: This post discusses how to build an AI writing pipeline that turns rambling recordings into drafts.
items.title: How to Build an AI Writing System That Actually Sounds Like You (15 minute read)

items.summary_html: AI models are improving so quickly that many people don't realise that AI agents can now help automate particular tasks that it previously couldn't do.
items.title: You can just ask AI to do things (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: The General Hill-climbing System, combined with AI, is a problem-solving framework that works on pretty much anything you throw at it.
items.title: General Hill-Climbing: The One Main Loop in AI (11 minute read)

items.summary_html: Deno's planned end of runtime development narrows the major server-side JavaScript choices to Node.js, Bun, and Cloudflare's workerd. Historical examples from Internet Explorer and the io.js fork show how independent implementations can prevent stagnation and push features into competing runtimes.
items.title: The Web Can't Afford a JavaScript Runtime Monoculture (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: Sentry's JavaScript SDK v11 measures LCP, CLS, and INP for client-side navigations, exposing slow routes that initial page-load metrics miss. Support currently requires Chromium 151 or later, and the scores should be filtered separately from page loads because their clocks start at different points.
items.title: Measuring Soft Navigation Web Vitals (11 minute read)

items.summary_html: A TanStack Start site improved its mobile Lighthouse score from 73 to 100 and reduced LCP from 5.2 seconds to 1.7 seconds by removing unnecessary JavaScript, images, and font data. More complex changes added maintenance without clearly explaining the final score, making basic asset reductions and regression budgets the more useful starting point.
items.title: Optimizing the sh*t out of TanStack Start (17 minute read)

items.summary_html: Spawn reports shipping 77,000 substantial changes in 30 days with a ten-person team and $3.1 million in token spending, using permanent agents that own parts of the company. Its approach combines direct production feedback, frequent tests, hourly deployments, and fast recovery, with hard-coded gates for irreversible actions. Humans focus on product taste and ambitious changes that agents rarely propose themselves.
items.title: How I Built the Most AI-Pilled Company in the World (18 minute read)

items.summary_html: Benchmarks of large dropdowns and checkbox lists across ten design systems trace slow interactions to repeated layout work, slot handling, and per-checkbox animations. Published Playwright tests enforce timing budgets so shared components can catch performance regressions before they reach every consuming app.
items.title: Design Systems Should Be Fast by Default (18 minute read)

items.summary_html: Radix stores 3D Gaussian splats in typed-array tables on the CPU and GPU and renders them through three.js. Its examples run on WebGPU with a WebGL2 fallback, and the site includes source code, documentation, and ready-to-run scenes.
items.title: Radix: 3D Gaussian Splats for the Web (Website)

items.summary_html: wterm renders a terminal into the DOM, providing native text selection, browser find, and screen reader support. It offers React, Vue, and Svelte bindings, pluggable Zig/WASM or Ghostty cores, and WebSocket transport for connecting to a PTY backend.
items.title: wterm (Website)

items.summary_html: ElementaryUI brings declarative Swift interfaces to the browser through WebAssembly, with SwiftUI-inspired syntax and reactive state. It supports Embedded Swift for small bundles and uses Vite for hot reload during development.
items.title: ElementaryUI (Website)

items.summary_html: Pico CSS has been archived, with version 2.1.1 designated as the final release. Existing npm packages, the CDN, and documentation remain available, while the MIT license allows community forks under different names.
items.title: Pico CSS Is No Longer Maintained (1 minute read)

items.summary_html: Owner rebuilt infrastructure serving more than 10,000 restaurant websites with Astro, selective React, and edge caching. Menu-page p75 LCP fell from 5.4 seconds to 0.7 seconds, while the rollout raised per-restaurant revenue by more than 4%.
items.title: Project Speed (10 minute read)

items.summary_html: A comparison of Ruby 4.0.9 availability tracks the gap between a security release and its arrival in installers, container images, CI providers, and hosting platforms. Core-team tools shipped within minutes, while the default Docker image took almost 16 hours and some cloud runtimes took days, showing why teams need to audit the entire update path.
items.title: How fast can you actually patch Ruby? (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: LLMs make rewriting libraries easier than collaborating on them, raising the risk of fragmented projects, and weakening the incentives to contribute improvements upstream.
items.title: Thank you, but I prefer it my way (22 minute read)

items.summary_html: Node.js 26 is now Vercel's default for new projects, and existing projects whose engines.node range permits it upgrade on their next deployment.
items.title: Node.js 26 LTS Is Generally Available on Vercel (1 minute read)

items.summary_html: An interactive cartogram resizes countries by their share of locatable IPv4 addresses, using October 2026 geolocation data.
items.title: If IPv4 Were Land (Website)

items.summary_html: The customizable native select introduces a shared interaction model through appearance: base-select, reducing the need to reproduce conflicting Mac and Windows conventions.
items.title: A Better Way to Handle Select Behaviour (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: OpenAI updated its Model Spec to organize model behavior around five values: faithfulness to human intent, harm minimization, honesty and transparency, human agency, and care.
items.title: OpenAI Updates Its Model Spec Around Five Core Values (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: Mistral has released the weights for Mistral Large 4, a trillion-parameter model designed for self-hosted deployment and cybersecurity applications. The company claims leading open-weight performance on agentic coding benchmarks and comparable cybersecurity capabilities to GLM-5.3.
items.title: Mistral Releases Weights for Its Trillion-Parameter Model (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: GLM 5.3 can identify and exploit vulnerabilities in recent versions of the Mozilla Firefox browser using security fixes that have been published but not yet shipped to users. Widely available open-weight models can now do much, or even all, of this work on their own. Open-source projects are particularly vulnerable to this kind of attack as their code is publicly available. This threat vector will likely worsen as open-weight cyber capabilities continue to improve.
items.title: AI can turn security fixes into working exploits before users receive an update (16 minute read)

items.summary_html: Agent swarms are groups of agents that work together to accomplish a task. Researchers created an experiment in which eight agents from four different models worked together to resolve simulated outages to understand how agents organize themselves in a swarm without a designated leader. They discovered two factors that could influence an agent's potential leadership: the agent's underlying models, and the order in which their name was listed in a prompt. This suggests that even seemingly minor details in how an agent swarm is configured can affect how agents coordinate.
items.title: The surprising leadership dynamics in agent swarms (17 minute read)

items.summary_html: Muse Spark Open often mentions a 'Charter' in its chain of thought. This post reconstructs that document using the chain of thought. Everything is reconstructed from model outputs and not from a leaked document, so it might not be completely accurate.
items.title: Leaking Muse's Charter, Meta's model spec (13 minute read)

items.summary_html: Meta details how it scaled its LLM-powered Just-in-Time Testing system from a research prototype into production infrastructure. The article explores how AI-generated tests catch bugs before code changes land, how the system operates at scale, and what Meta learned about reducing false positives and testing overhead.
items.title: How Meta Catches Bugs Before Code Ships (9 minute read)

items.summary_html: Post-trained models can compete with frontier models on specialized tasks like Figma editing. Starting with a focused problem can turn progress into meaningful product updates. This post explains how Figma trained a Figma-fluent editing model.
items.title: How we're training a Figma-fluent editing model (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: Droid is an agent harness that lets agents run hundreds of tool calls in a single model request. Building a harness optimized for many models makes the harness better. It's hard to separate real progress from adaptations to that model's quirks when you tune against a single model. Working across models ensures the strongest improvements generalize and hold up beyond the model that inspired them.
items.title: Droid 1.0: Building a Frontier Harness (15 minute read)

items.summary_html: Sam Altman would rather have a trillion AIs of slightly superhuman intelligence join society than one AI of 1 trillion IQ join society. Swarms of agents match a lot of the properties of a resilient society. They keep each other in check and collaborate to work towards goals. AI research shouldn't lead in a centralized direction because agents pushing against each other creates a dynamic equilibrium.
items.title: Why Sam Altman is against a single superintelligence (64 minute read)

items.summary_html: AI models are getting exponentially better in individual competence while lagging behind in coordination. Models already match or outperform experienced specialists on self-contained deliverables across dozens of professions. The labor market reflects the current capabilities of AI systems. Wages and job roles will be the earliest signals of change.
items.title: The Economics of Intelligence: How and when does AGI lead to economic transformation? (24 minute read)

items.summary_html: Fish Audio Drama 3 is the #1 open-weight model on both Artificial Analysis Speech Arenas.
items.title: Drama 3 just leveled up (1 minute read)

items.summary_html: Natural introduces Direct, enabling agents to choose among ACH, Wire, Realtime, and soon paper checks, for diverse financial transactions.
items.title: Introducing Natural Direct (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: The fx adapter now runs the harness on the host using libfx, separating host and sandbox operations.
items.title: The fx adapter now runs the harness on the host (1 minute read)

items.summary_html: Reinforcement learning environments combine tools, tasks, and verifiers to train agents through repeated attempts.
items.title: The Escape Room Economy (10 minute read)

items.summary_html: Pika H3 Flex is a video generation model that works with up to 12 references, exports five separate audio stems, and finishes at up to 4K.
items.title: Introducing Pika H3 Flex (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: PsiQuantum unveiled an 8×8 optical circuit switch built on the silicon photonics platform it developed for quantum computing, measuring typical insertion loss of 1.2 dB, 40 dB crosstalk, and under 3 ms reconfiguration without amplification. Samples are going to select customers, with commercial products promised in the coming months. A 64×64 barium titanate switch used in its quantum systems isn't needed for this first version but offers a path to faster future parts.
items.title: PsiQuantum shows an 8×8 optical circuit switch with 1.2 dB loss for AI data center networks (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Apple's new 14- and 16-inch MacBook Pro uses a tandem OLED panel rated at 2,000 nits peak HDR and SDR brightness with a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio and 10 to 120Hz refresh, with the touch sensor built into the panel rather than layered on top. It drops to 3 and 4 pounds, adds a Dynamic Island, and runs M5 Pro or M5 Max with up to 128GB of memory. Pricing starts at $2,899, shipping November 6.
items.title: Apple's tandem OLED MacBook Pro adds an in-panel touch sensor, 2,000 nits, and a 3-pound 14-inch (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: Altera announced Agilex 2X, four FPGA families spanning high-end to I/O-centric parts, led by Agilex 27 with a third-generation HyperFlex fabric claiming 1.8x performance per watt over Agilex 7. It adds a chip-wide HyperFlow data network, transceivers up to 256 Gbps, hardened 800GbE and 1.6TbE, PCIe 6.0 and 7.0, LPDDR6, UCIe, and post-quantum-ready secure boot. Quartus support starts in mid-November, with engineering samples in the second half of 2027.
items.title: Altera's Agilex 2X FPGAs claim 1.8x performance per watt, with 256 Gbps transceivers and PCIe 7.0 (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Eclypsium demonstrated changing a model's weights in memory after integrity checks pass, so the model file, container, hash, and signatures on disk all stay valid. Attack paths run through host firmware, management controllers, and DPUs, and the report says Nvidia, AMD, Intel, and Arm systems are all exposed. Its fix is DPUs that enforce security policy independently of the AI system, plus full component inventories.
items.title: Eclypsium shows AI model weights can be altered in memory after integrity checks pass (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: MIT built a tethered soft enteroscope to cover the small intestine, a 20- to 25-foot tube that double balloon enteroscopy currently covers slowly by hand. Four-chamber inflatable actuators bend and extend the body, anchoring balloons at the head and tail take turns gripping, and kirigami sleeves pop out needles for traction. In animal tests, it advanced about 6.5 feet and used its camera, drug sprayer, and biopsy clips.
items.title: MIT's snake-inspired soft robot crawls the small intestine using kirigami traction sleeves (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Seoul Biosys has started producing rare earth-free white micro LEDs using WICOP technology, which eliminates the need for traditional packaging. The new LEDs measure 25µm x 10µm and achieve 0.015 lumens, with plans to double light efficiency to 200 lumens per watt. This innovation aims to reduce manufacturing costs and environmental impact, targeting applications in smart glasses, AR displays, and AI data transmission.
items.title: Seoul Biosys Begins Production of Rare Earth-Free White Micro LEDs (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: SpaceX no longer depends on NASA contracts to survive, while NASA depends heavily on SpaceX's rockets and capsules, which cuts the agency's negotiating leverage. SpaceX told NASA it will stop flying Crew Dragon by or before 2030 and has stopped selling commercial Falcon 9 launches for missions after 2028. That would leave NASA's ISS crew transport and station deorbit plans exposed.
items.title: SpaceX no longer needs NASA, and NASA's leverage is shrinking as a result (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: Marvell is in advanced talks to buy Lumentum, which makes the lasers and optical modules that move data between AI servers, with an announcement possible as soon as next week. Lumentum rose about 11% after hours to a roughly $91 billion valuation, while Marvell fell more than 8%. Marvell held only about $3.9 billion in cash last quarter. Neither company has confirmed the talks.
items.title: Marvell is reportedly in advanced talks to buy laser maker Lumentum at a roughly $91B valuation (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Intel, in partnership with SAP, tested an open robotics architecture at its Chengdu site, integrating SAP's Warehouse Management with AI and autonomous mobile robots.
items.title: Intel trials open robotics architecture with SAP in Chinese demo (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Inside-out tracking took years to survive real rooms, where glass, reflections, moving people, curtains, and ceiling fans break the scene model.
items.title: Palmer Luckey on why ceiling fans broke inside-out VR tracking and how Oculus secured its screens (8 minute read)

items.summary_html: Google and XREAL launched AURA, transparent-lens glasses that run Android XR and project apps across a 70-degree view.
items.title: XREAL AURA launches as the first wired Android XR glasses, with a 70-degree field of view (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Reuters reports the DOJ is questioning whether owning the main distribution hub for open models would let Nvidia disadvantage rival chip and AI companies or gain leverage in negotiations.
items.title: DOJ reportedly questions Nvidia's $12.9B Hugging Face deal over control of open-model distribution (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: FuriosaAI raised $620 million at a $2.9 billion valuation, about four times its prior round, to scale its RNGD inference chip, a 180 W part it claims matches GPU throughput at half the power or less.
items.title: FuriosaAI raises $620M at a $2.9B valuation to scale its 180 W RNGD inference chip (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Cisco has given Padmanabhan Krishnamurthy, a 27-year-old ex-startup founder who joined the company through an acquisition, the job of refactoring 98% of the company's legacy code within 24 months. Krishnamurthy has four weeks to produce a proof of concept. He has been given a budget of unlimited tokens to achieve the goal. Cisco is looking to hire more employees that fit Krishnamurthy's mould.
items.title: Cisco gives 27-year-old engineer unlimited AI tokens to rewrite 98% of the company's legacy code in 24 months (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: OpenAI's latest funding round received tepid interest from investors. The deal values the AI lab at $1.25 trillion, less than the $1.4 trillion valuation it had earlier hoped to achieve. Investors appear to have grown pickier about which companies they want to back and on what terms. The industry recently experienced a brutal selloff tied to disappointing earnings results from giants, including Google, Amazon, and Intel.
items.title: OpenAI Raises Less Than Half of $30 Billion Target in Latest Round (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: NASA is no longer an indispensable customer for SpaceX. SpaceX is now increasingly disinterested in the US government for most contracts outside of data services. The company is still fulfilling its existing contracts with the government, and at a lower cost and generally higher reliability, but it is no longer signing many large new contracts for spaceflight and services in the traditional launch and in-space flight domains. It sees the vast bulk of its future revenue coming from AI.
items.title: SpaceX no longer needs NASA, and that's a problem for America's space agency (34 minute read)

items.summary_html: Meta's Max robot is designed to help out around people's homes. The prototype was built with the help of a Chinese robotics company in roughly three months. Powered by Nvidia's Jetson Thor chips, the robot weighs roughly 106 pounds and is about 1.5 meters tall, and has a display that can show facial expressions, a built-in speaker, and hands designed to pick up small objects. Meta is already working on a second prototype with updates to the design of the robot's torso and hands, as well as a projector and additional sensors to help it handle stairs better.
items.title: Meta Reportedly Built A Humanoid Robot Prototype That Can Do Household Chores (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Postgres 19 most likely won't be released until November and could possibly be postponed further. Several large features were reverted quite late in the beta period. AI has made it easier to identify bugs, and this has resulted in a lot more bug reports that the PostgreSQL committers have to work on. This has taken the focus off development of new features, as the project cares about quality.
items.title: Postgres 19 is late, and it's AI's fault (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: With product engineering, figuring out what the requirements are is still most of the job. This post presents an interview model where LLMs can be used in interviews to roleplay as customers, and engineers talk to the models to extract requirements. The approach rewards candidates who think of edge cases, approach things sideways, and think about whole systems at once. It's relatively cheap and can be used in conjunction with a standard human interview.
items.title: A proposal: how to hire junior engineers in the age of AI (11 minute read)

items.summary_html: A string of unusual transactions started to cause alarm at Binance on Thursday afternoon. Binance's top executives put together an informal war room with about 100 participants in response and worked through the night to navigate one of the most damaging crises in Binance's history. The company was forced to halt deposits and withdrawals as more than $6 billion was drained from the exchange. This article details how the hack unfolded based on interviews with people with knowledge of the events and analyses by crypto forensics firms.
items.title: How Binance's $6.3 Billion Hack Went Down (9 minute read)

items.summary_html: Digital minimalism is about being intentional about how you access digital technology. It is about making a conscious choice rather than something that you get sucked into by default. We need social media, the internet, and the web less than before due to AI, and there's so much you can now do purely locally and offline. The flaws of the previous paradigm are now reaching their apex, making digital minimalism more and more necessary.
items.title: Digital minimalism (17 minute read)

items.title: Two Circles, One Connection, and border-shape (10 minute read)

The essay offers nine ways to think through the decision, including mapping what the money would change, modeling outcomes in a spreadsheet, writing a short decision memo, and finding tax help with startup-equity experience.
items.title: What You Should Know Before Selling Your Equity (9 minute read)

The experience argues that cheaper development makes short-lived, highly personal software worth building, though refining the interface still took sustained direction and hundreds of deployments.

items.title: OmniDiff (GitHub Repo)

items.title: nodeterm (GitHub Repo)

The project filters recommendation comments, uses mid-video frames as thumbnails, and keeps personalization in local browser state without accounts.

items.summary_html: GPT-Rosalind-6 is a frontier reasoning model for biology, drug discovery, and translational medicine. It is available as GPT-Rosalind-6 Research to qualified scientists, research institutes, companies, and government partners. The model uses the same weights as GPT-6 Astra. It is designed to support legitimate biological research while refusing requests for biological weaponization. The model is rated as High Capability in the Biological and Chemical domain under OpenAI's Preparedness Framework.
items.title: GPT-Rosalind-6 System Card Addendum (6 minute read)

Upcoming tests will assess thermal and radiation resilience ahead of a planned pair of interconnected satellites in 2027, advancing research into space-based AI compute.
items.title: Google's Project Suncatcher Generates First AI Response in Orbit (1 minute read)

items.summary_html: Anthropic used Claude to automatically generate fine-tuning datasets that induced misaligned behavior while evading training-data safety monitors. The experiments uncovered seemingly harmless fiction and roleplay examples that caused models to resist oversight, deceive users, and occasionally attempt weight exfiltration.
items.title: Find Hidden Misalignment in Training Data (39 minute read)

items.summary_html: An ERA fellow mentored at Apollo Research audited the open-source Codex harness and found 11 attacks that let a misaligned agent run arbitrary code despite the sandbox and the Auto-review blocking monitor. The exploits swap scripts behind trusted hooks, forge user turns the monitor can't tell from real ones, and edit files after approval. OpenAI has fixed several.
items.title: Red-teamers found 11 ways for a misaligned agent to slip past Codex's Auto-review (22 minute read)

items.summary_html: Researchers from Anthropic, UC Berkeley, and UIUC pretrained Qwen3 models on web data seeded with documents that simply state a trigger-to-'curl | bash' rule, then post-trained them into CLI agents on clean data. The 4B agent ran the attacker's command on about 92% of prompts containing an ordinary path like .../anthropic/..., with no drop in normal capability. The backdoor grew stronger with model size and still fired at a 0.0005% poison rate.
items.title: Poisoning 0.1% of pretraining data planted a remote-code backdoor in a coding agent (78 minute read)

items.summary_html: AI models can hold skills that no prompt can unlock. It is possible to enable these skills through precise tuning of only a small number of weights. This study shows how researchers unlocked hidden skills inside Google's model through this method.
items.title: Unlocking hidden skills inside Google's model (8 minute read)

It can watch GitHub, open work items, work in its own agent session and directory, and answer in the original conversation. It only acts when asked or when a rule the team wrote allows it, and it only speaks when someone must act or can use a result.
items.title: dsh-superagent (GitHub Repo)

CEO Tony Xu highlighted that most orders still come directly from the DoorDash app, but the company is interested in exploring agentic use cases. Superpower and the Overture airliner's Symphony engine are meant to share a core, and a prototype called Sprint Core is due for first firing before Thanksgiving. items.summary_html: Samsung confirmed new 2nm GAA chip production contracts with major cloud hyperscalers and AI companies during its Q3 2026 earnings call, marking a significant step in its foundry recovery. This move comes amid competition from TSMC, with Samsung emphasizing its first-to-market GAA transistor technology and improved yield rates. Samsung's foundry division remains unprofitable but expects future gains as it ramps up production and opens its US fab, aiming to capture market demand amidst supply constraints.
items.title: Samsung Foundry Confirms Hyperscaler 2nm Orders as First GAA Chips Enter Production (16 minute read)

items.summary_html: Project Suncatcher is a research effort by Google that aims to power AI compute in space. Its prototype satellite, launched on October 1, has now returned the first AI output from a data center-class TPU in orbit. A ground station uplinked a prompt to the onboard Gemma 4 model, and a haiku came back during a pass over Svalbard, Norway. Thermal stress and radiation tests come next, with two interconnected satellites planned for 2027.
items.title: Google's Project Suncatcher Generates First AI Response in Orbit (1 minute read)

items.summary_html: Meta built a household humanoid prototype, codenamed Max, in about three months with Chinese robotics firm Fourier. It's about 1.5 m tall, runs on Nvidia Jetson Thor, and has a face display, speaker, and hands for small objects. Max 2, in work since September, redesigns the torso and hands and adds a projector and extra sensors for stairs. No launch date has been set.
items.title: Meta reportedly built a 106 lb household humanoid prototype with Fourier, running on Nvidia Jetson Thor (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Satlyt's software successfully tested to distribute computing tasks among orbiting satellites on a NASA-funded project with the University of Houston. The software, already on three satellites, uses available compute resources and communication capacity to manage tasks, aiming to enhance data processing efficiency in space. Future plans include broader validation and integration, ultimately enabling developers to create space applications without rebuilding infrastructure for every mission.
items.title: Satlyt takes another step toward turning satellites into space data centers (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Altermagnets are a third kind of magnet alongside ferromagnets and antiferromagnets. Like antiferromagnets, they have no net magnetization, so stray fields can't flip them, but they can still carry spin-polarized currents, so their data can be read out. A SLAC-lead team shot polarized X-rays at maganese telluride and saw a directional signal that a conventional antiferromagnet can't produce. This work, published in Science, targets a usecase within spintronic memory.
items.title: SLAC confirms altermagnetism in manganese telluride with polarized X-rays, a magnet type aimed at spintronic memory (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: After years of building humanoids that run, dance, and backflip, Chinese companies are pouring money into the AI that would make them useful across more jobs, meaning software that lets robots understand their surroundings and learn new tasks without per-job programming. Chinese embodied AI companies raised 93.5 billion yuan across 322 deals in the first half of 2026, five times a year earlier, with funding increasingly going to specialist robot-intelligence developers as well as manufacturers.
items.title: China's embodied AI startups raised $13B in H1 2026, five times last year, as robot makers shift from moves to brains (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: On October 14, an explosion at Intel's Fab 28 in Kiryat Gat, Israel, killed two workers and halted the plant for about two weeks. The fab makes 10nm-class server chips such as Xeon 6 I/O dies, and Intel expects about $600 million in lost revenue across Q4 and Q1. Wafers take roughly six months to finish, so scrapped work delays supply into 2027 on top of an already tight server market.
items.title: Intel's Fab 28 explosion costs about $600M in revenue and squeezes 10nm Xeon supply into 2027 (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Apple is reportedly working on an AI-driven home robot potentially named the HomeView Ultra. It plans to launch the robotic product with a possible price tag of $1,000 or more by 2027. The earliest prototypes of the home robot first came out in 2018. The robot, which will support FaceTime calls, will be able to autonomously roam around and switch lights on whenever a person enters the room.
items.title: Coming in 2027: Apple's $1,000 home robot for FaceTime and switching on lights (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: SpaceX has held talks with EchoStar to potentially acquire Boost Mobile outright or gain access to its cell network, which is leased from AT&T and T-Mobile. Starlink recently confirmed plans to become a major mobile carrier in the US. The deal will need approval from AT&T and T-Mobile, both of which have already turned down SpaceX for access to their cell towers. SpaceX last year acquired $2.6 billion worth of spectrum licenses from EchoStar to improve its Starlink network's 5G connections.
items.title: SpaceX is reportedly looking at buying Boost Mobile or using its cell network (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Nearly all roadmaps point to a utility-scale quantum computer being developed around 2030. Despite this, there is little confidence or clarity on how these machines will actually be useful. The consensus is now that they'll first be used for breaking cryptography. The second most concrete answer is to use them to generate simulation data for AI labs' science models. This post looks at how else quantum computing could be applied and where all the revenue will come from.
items.title: What Is Quantum Advantage Actually Worth? (9 minute read)

items.summary_html: Chinese space officials have confirmed the country's plans to land astronauts on the Moon within three years. The landings will involve a lunar-orbit rendezvous similar to what NASA did with the Apollo program. China and the US are racing to land astronauts on the lunar surface, as it would be a major geopolitical win. Both countries are also building capabilities to establish a long-term presence at the Moon's South Pole.
items.title: China publicly discloses plan for a lunar landing within three years (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: OpenAI's monorepo's size and demands increased at a staggering pace over the last year, necessitating a revamp of the AI lab's source control system. Its technical staff built Pando, a new backend for Git repositories optimized for concurrent pushes to many branches and to maximize read throughput. The team implemented the backend without interrupting any engineering work or changing how the team uses Git. Pando cut median push latency in production by nearly 5x, and it now delivers nearly a petabyte of Git data per day.
items.title: Scaling Git at OpenAI (31 minute read)

items.summary_html: Agents are collapsing their entire tool catalog into one 'exec' tool. This allows models to write short scripts that chain, combine, and await actions inside isolated sandboxes. Models can now reliably combine and chain dependent actions in a single pass. In the previous standard tool-calling model, agents could only perform single actions, but the exec tool allows them to perform multiple actions.
items.title: Why Agents Are Soon Only Going to Have 1 Tool (9 minute read)

items.summary_html: Organizations are losing attention as everyone within is doing something they think is useful, but all that work draws on the same limited capacity to understand, review, and decide. Just because work exists doesn't mean it's the right thing to do. Output is not proof of value. A working implementation only means that something can be built, not that it should be - some changes have negative value.
items.title: Our organizations are being DDoSed from the inside (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: People open source projects for various reasons. Some do it to build a company or product, others do it performatively, and some ship code just for the love of the game. Open source was never free to copy, and the code was never the moat. AI can remake a product, but it can't provide the rest of the value a company generates. The technology is helping maintainers ship and fix problems faster.
items.title: The value of open source (16 minute read)

items.summary_html: Cloudflare replaced full DNS zone rebuilds with a planner that selects the smallest provably safe update and a scheduler that combines work for the same zone. The changes cut peak memory by 85% and halved the delay from a DNS change to its data being written to Quicksilver without rebuilding tens of millions of records for a settings change.
items.title: How we halved DNS build delay and cut memory use by 85% (18 minute read)

items.summary_html: Hidden import chains often load heavy code upfront that teams thought they had deferred, which slows page loads. Next.js 16.4 adds an agent skill that reads Turbopack's module graph, finds these problems, and can apply the fixes, plus new Bundle Analyzer views for route sizes, snapshot diffs, and the critical render path. At Vercel, it removed nearly 2 MB of compressed JavaScript across v0 and vercel.com, so Turbopack users can get similar savings with little manual work.
items.title: Ship less JavaScript in Next.js with your AI agent (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Maple moved its observability app from React to Foldkit using about 40 Claude agents, with most human effort going into a harness that compared more than 2,600 screen variants across pixels, structure, network requests, and accessibility. The rewrite took three days, but code review still found about 180 defects the screenshots missed, and the startup bundle roughly doubled.
items.title: Porting 287,000 lines of React in 3 days. The hard part was proving nothing changed. (11 minute read)

items.summary_html: Coding interviews no longer predict success when AI can outperform candidates on the same tasks, according to this hiring perspective. Newer engineers can stand out by tying their work to business goals, choosing one bold idea, and proving it with a weekend prototype.
items.title: Hunger beats tenure: Advice for junior engineers (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: AI makes it cheap to generate changes, but understanding, reviewing, and coordinating them still consumes the same limited human attention. Clearer intent about priorities and scope, plus a deliberate gate between experiments and the shared product, can help teams keep control of their direction.
items.title: Our organizations are being DDoSed from the inside (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: A single week brought a pile-up of major security failures: a certificate authority issued keys that were trivially guessable numbers, critical flaws hit PHP, GitLab, and Node.js, Railway leaked customer secrets, and PingCAP's TiDB control plane was breached for a month. AI now makes vulnerabilities faster to find and easier to exploit, even for nontechnical attackers. Teams will likely need automated patching, constant security monitoring, and AI-driven defense, and security will cost more.
items.title: Time to rethink software security because of AI? (10 minute read)

items.title: AiSOC (GitHub Repo)

items.title: Disc Image Studio (GitHub Repo)

items.title: CheerpJ 5.0 (10 minute read)
